_comment: HIMMEL-1040 named plugin-profile registry. Resolved by plugin-profiles.mjs into an enabledPlugins map, injected per-dispatch via `claude --settings` (lever-b, highest non-managed precedence) so lane workers run lean while the operator's own ~/.claude stays full. Design: handovers/yotamleo/himmel/specs/design/2026-07-16-himmel-1040-agent-provider-plugin-profiles-design.md. FLOOR is inviolable (harness-operational: dispatch/search/handover). CATALOG is the known plugin universe the resolver sets false for anything a profile does not enable — a COMPLETE map is correct whether Claude Code merges or replaces enabledPlugins. DENY-BY-DEFAULT BEYOND THE CATALOG: the resolver also disables every id passed via opts.installed (the caller's LIVE plugin universe — the spawn scripts pass readEnabledPluginIds over the child's effective config dir + every ancestor settings layer), so a plugin installed/enabled on the machine but absent from CATALOG is still turned off for a lane. Only a CATALOG-ONLY caller (one that passes no opts.installed) retains the staleness gap — such an id stays unmentioned and inherits its enabled state until added to CATALOG (the HIMMEL-819 class; a pre-commit floor/catalog check is the tracked follow-up). disallowedTools (per-profile, optional) is SCHEMA-ONLY as of HIMMEL-1461 T2.1b — nothing consumes it yet; the producer (a --disallowedTools CLI flag through the claudex builder, via a second resolver export) is T2.3.
_comment_lean_skills_swap: HIMMEL-3064: superpowers@claude-plugins-official and mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official are DROPPED from catalog (and lean-skills@himmel added to base, so every profile inherits it) because, measured over 1628 local transcripts, those two always-on plugins carried ~2.2k tok of skill/agent listing into every session for skills almost never invoked (superpowers: 4 invocations ever across 14 skills; mattpocock-skills: zero across 11). lean-skills@himmel vendors verbatim just the subset actually used -- 11 of superpowers' 14 skills (the reference closure of the 4 himmel invokes) plus grilling from mattpocock/skills -- so a session pays for 13 skill listings instead of 25. Per-skill enable/disable does not exist in Claude Code settings, so plugin membership was the only lever; see marketplace/plugins/lean-skills/README.md for the vendoring/drift-detection contract and scripts/lanes/vendored-skill-dupes.mjs (+ himmel-doctor C37) for the duplicate-enablement guard if an adopter turns an upstream plugin back on alongside it.
_comment_gateAllow: HIMMEL-2959: permissions.allow is checked before the auto-mode classifier; deny rules still win and are never emitted or edited here. Guards: merge-on-green checks console GO, certified green head and unresolved threads; queue-lock checks ownership/release tokens; inbox-send validates a bounded local append; write-verdicts validates verdict inputs; clear-cr-marker limits cleanup to branch markers; panel-first-pass records critic evidence; HIMMEL-3338 (operator ruling 2026-09-21: legs may send review diffs to Codex) adds the rest of /pr-check's external-critic steps — docs-audit-panel with a tail, codex-adv-kickoff, codex-adv-harvest, doc-freshness-advisory and `known-findings.sh --diff` as exact literals — and HIMMEL-3359 adds /pr-check step 0's himmel-lane entry `bash scripts/cr/pr-check-context.sh` as an exact literal (permitted by the runbooks ONLY on a diff whose `git diff --name-only origin/main -- scripts/cr/` check exits 0 and prints nothing — that condition is the trust root, not this rule; the script's own hand-off of a non-anchor copy to the anchor's copy is defense in depth, since branch bytes could delete it) — and every one is a RELATIVE literal because the matcher compares the command text: /pr-check spells the call `bash scripts/cr/<x>.sh` when step 0's himmel_dir equals its repo, and the absolute `<himmel_dir>` spelling never matched any of these rules; ledger-append validates local evidence rows; check-ci reports forge checks; push rules are omitted because a branch-suffix wildcard also admits trailing --no-verify and skips the git hooks it relies on; pushes stay on the classifier path until a proven deny pair exists (HIMMEL-2962). quiet-run itself runs arbitrary argv, so never allow its blanket prefix: only the literal suite label + an enumerated directory + test-*.sh is admitted. A suite run that wants the deterministic rule uses the label suite; any other label simply falls back to today's classifier path — no regression. The matcher's handling of the env prefix and of a tail glob is unproven until the console's first native --profile leg-impl dispatch. Directory wildcards were dropped because they can absorb a different program before a fake test suffix. Node quiet-run rules are omitted entirely (directory globs/path traversal); node suites remain on the classifier path. scripts/lanes/ has no tracked direct test-*.sh and is omitted. Only the four leg-shaped profiles opt in; operator/user/bare keep their original output. Claudex profile composition is separate (HIMMEL-2962); sanitize_settings preserves operator-managed user-scope rules, not these native profile rules. Live proof 2026-09-12 (HIMMEL-2967 leg N201, first native --profile leg-impl dispatch): the env-prefix + tail-glob rule shape ran a real suite with no prompt, AND the traversal shape scripts/hooks/test-x/../../evil.sh also ran (rc=127, no denial) — so on this build the allow path does not stop `..` traversal; the structural control is quiet-run.sh's own path guard (HIMMEL-2967).

leg-impl._comment: HIMMEL-2830 / HIMMEL-2928 lever 1. Resolves to the same plugin set as lane-impl TODAY and that is deliberate, not an oversight: the differentiator is contextBudget. A headed leg re-pays its whole fixed context on every API call of a session that runs for hours, so its budget is the measured leg target (35000), not the lane-worker default (45000). Do NOT "dedupe" this into lane-impl — a lane worker and a headed leg are different callers with different floors, and headed-arm-leg.sh --profile names this one. Sibling profiles leg-docs and leg-upstream were designed and DROPPED: leg-docs would resolve to bare AND break /pr-check (its CR gate dispatches the pr-review-toolkit-himmel:code-reviewer agent, which a docs leg needs too), and /drift-fix, /fork-resync and /upstream-file are repo-local .claude/commands/*.md, not plugin-borne, so leg-upstream would be a second name for this exact manifest. mcpServers (HIMMEL-2935, lever 1 second half): --strict-mcp-config strips EVERY MCP server not named here, including plugin-bundled ones — qmd is named because it is the one MCP tool this profile's own plugin set (pr-review-toolkit-himmel + the floor's qmd@himmel) actually needs; graphify/obsidian-vault/context7 are USER-level servers a leg never touches. MEASURED (RED control, HIMMEL-2935): removing them saved only 2.5k of first-turn context (73.0k to 70.5k) — they were NOT the bulk of the floor; #642's ~40k tool/MCP-schema estimate is dominated by built-in tool schemas and skill/agent listings this lever cannot touch. Lever 1 is exhausted at that number; do not chase the remaining floor here.

telegram._comment: HIMMEL-2961. Wired ONLY at the bridge dispatch (scripts/telegram/poller.ts's makeRunFn/runOnce, the sole per-message cold `claude` spawn) — the entry-point inventory found two other Telegram-adjacent spawn sites and both are out of scope: auto-action.ts's dispatchAutoAction spawns no claude at all (it shells out to fixed scripts), and hermes is its own interpreter, dormant, with no plugin-profile seam to wire. enable mirrors lane-content (obsidian-triage + claude-obsidian cover the actual Telegram workload — clip/harvest/archive/triage/media-enrich commands — plus pr-review-toolkit-himmel restated for audit-clarity though base already carries it); telegram-himmel@himmel is deliberately EXCLUDED even though it is the bridge's own plugin — its .mcp.json defines an MCP server also named telegram (gated by HIMMEL_MCP_TELEGRAM/TELEGRAM_OWN_POLLER) that launches a second poller-adjacent process, which would be self-referential/recursive inside the very session the live poller spawned. luna-correlate@himmel is excluded as unrelated (health-factor correlation, not content work). mcpServers names only qmd — of every plugin in this profile's enable+base+floor union, qmd is the sole one that bundles an MCP server this profile's own plugin set actually needs (luna-correlate and telegram-himmel are the only other two plugins in the whole marketplace that bundle one at all, and both are excluded above); --strict-mcp-config then strips every USER-level server (graphify/obsidian-vault/context7/etc.) the bridge never touches. MEASURED (profile-context-probe.mjs, HIMMEL-2961): baseline (no --settings, today's live bridge) = 33440-33493 first-turn tokens across runs; telegram profile measured=32541 against contextBudget=45000 (delta -952) — the injected lean set is already BELOW the unleaned baseline, so the win here is deny-by-default correctness (no ambient full ~/.claude leak into an unattended bridge run) rather than a token reduction.

console-relay._comment: HIMMEL-2975: Sonnet relay of a split console. No plugins, no MCP servers. drop removes every non-floor id registry.base now carries (pr-review-toolkit-himmel@himmel, and lean-skills@himmel as of HIMMEL-3064 -- a relay has no business brainstorming/TDD-ing, it only forwards) so this profile resolves to floor-only, same shape as bare but with gateAllow. Its write-deny hook (guard-relay-writes.sh) keys off HIMMEL_CONSOLE_RELAY, not this profile.

console-judge._comment: HIMMEL-3133 / design §3.2: a judge session, launched via headed-arm-leg.sh --judge ("the judge is a leg"). drop removes the same two non-floor ids console-relay drops above (pr-review-toolkit-himmel@himmel, lean-skills@himmel) -- a judge reads and writes a verdict, it does not implement or ship. Deliberately no gateAllow, unlike console-relay: a judge's few gate-shaped calls (inbox-send.sh, queue-lock.sh, write-verdicts.sh) take the ordinary classifier path rather than being pre-approved wholesale -- its custody rule is "transport is the disk" (a verdict file), not a permission grant, so this name does NOT belong in plugin-profiles.mjs's LEG_PROFILES set (:29, its only reader) and that file is not touched for this profile. mcpServers names only qmd, same reasoning as leg-impl/telegram above: the one MCP tool a judge's evidence-gathering actually needs; graphify/obsidian-vault/context7 are USER-level servers a judge never touches.
